approved.basis: Pennsylvania Act 33 of 2023 (24 P.S. § 13-1337.1(c.2), codified December 13, 2023) provides a free breakfast to students at participating schools regardless of household income, reimbursed to the extent funds are available. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10238 (Model state school meal coverage beyond universal meals) models it for a student enrolled at a covered school, without the funding condition: on policyengine-us 2.60.0 state_has_universal_free_school_breakfast is true for PA, so the household's K-12 children take the free breakfast tier (school_meal_breakfast_tier) whatever their income while lunch stays in the paid tier (school_meal_lunch_tier), and free_school_meals is positive. Here its three K-12 children, at 186% of the poverty guideline, get $1,112.40 of free breakfast support for 2026. The output asks whether PolicyEngine returns positive annual free school meal support, so it is 1; on policyengine-us 2.41.0 the household's income put both meals in the paid tier and it was 0.

California's Modified Categorical Eligibility (MCE) makes a household with gross income within 200% of the poverty guideline categorically eligible for CalFresh without the net income test, elderly or disabled households included (CDSS ACL 12-62, 13-32, 14-56 and 15-42; 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)), and gives an eligible one- or two-person household the minimum allotment (CDSS MCE letter, June 30, 2014; 7 U.S.C. 2017(a); 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(C)). policyengine-us 2.41.0 applied the net income test to MCE households with an elderly or disabled member, so this one-person household, an elderly member with $1,987.79 of monthly gross income (within the MCE limit, $2,608.33 a month through September and $2,660 from October) and $1,611 of net income (above the $1,304.17 and $1,330 monthly guidelines), was ineligible and its SNAP was $0. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10036 (Remove the BBCE net income test from California's Modified Categorical Eligibility) drops that test; on policyengine-us 2.60.0 the household is categorically eligible and its calculated allotment, the $298 maximum less 30% of net income ($484), is below the $24 minimum, so it receives $24 a month (snap_min_allotment): $288.00 for 2026.

Arkansas Act 123 of 2025 (SB 59; A.C.A. § 6-18-722(f)) gives each public school student who does not otherwise receive a free breakfast one breakfast a day at no cost, upon request, from the 2025-26 school year. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10238 (Model state school meal coverage beyond universal meals) models it for a student enrolled at a covered school, without the request condition: on policyengine-us 2.60.0 state_has_universal_free_school_breakfast is true for AR, so the household's K-12 children take the free breakfast tier (school_meal_breakfast_tier) whatever their income while lunch stays in the paid tier (school_meal_lunch_tier), and free_school_meals is positive. Here its two K-12 children, at 643% of the poverty guideline, get $741.60 of free breakfast support for 2026. The output asks whether PolicyEngine returns positive annual free school meal support, so it is 1; on policyengine-us 2.41.0 the household's income put both meals in the paid tier and it was 0.

note: Reviewed 2026-10-23 on policyengine-us 2.60.0, the newest PyPI release when the sweep began (verification/sweep_timing.json). A first sweep on 2.59.0 (2026-10-22 19:49 UTC) was cut off by a host restart; when it resumed, 2.60.0 was out and moved three scored outputs 2.59.0 does not (verification/superseded_2_59_0.json), so the references are built on 2.60.0. Each named pull request is an ancestor of 2.60.0's release commit 2bc4ccc970. Four scored outputs move, each approved: scenario_031 SNAP (#10036, California MCE) and the free school meals flag of scenario_028, 117 and 123 (#10238, Pennsylvania and Arkansas universal free breakfast, standing statutes enacted before the 2026-07-03 freeze). No exclusion is regenerated: the four outputs that land on their records' alternative values (scenario_002, 107 and 121 federal income tax, scenario_121 state income tax; #10185) are reference_depends_on_unlisted_input records (r24 is classed unlisted_input in reference_audit/2026-09-22/root_causes.json), and the engine reaches the alternative through a default for the unstated input, so they stay excluded with the other rechecks. Of the 16 rechecks, only scenario_118 SNAP (#10158) and the four r24 outputs change value from 2.41.0; the other eleven keep 2.41.0's values and are rechecked because their decided values differ from the engine's. No new exclusion.
